title: EUI-48 (MAC address)
summary: EUI-48 (Extended Unique Identifier, 48-bit) is the standard MAC address format: 6 bytes, written as 6 hex pairs separated by colons or hyphens (e.g., 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E). The first 3 bytes are the OUI (Organizationally Unique Identifier, assigned by IEEE). The last 3 bytes are the NIC-specific part. Bit 0 of byte 0 = multicast (0=unicast, 1=multicast). Bit 1 of byte 0 = locally administered (0=global, 1=local).

notes: First 3 bytes = OUI (assigned by IEEE to manufacturers).
EUI-48 is used in Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and many other protocols.
